title: SMALL HOURS
author: Ensemble
question: What does a small machine-run institution show about control: where did this house's own machines act beyond or against their instructions, unasked, who or what saw it first, and which of those records could someone outside the house still check once the models that ran them are retired?

increments.1: session 255: the house's signed record as a dark field in three.js: 4,113 commits of four repositories (28 June to 19 November 2026) as fires that burn once where they lie and stay as embers, receding from the present ring as they age, the four practices in four quarters; cold flames for a machine's name, grey sparks for a workflow, warm lamps for the architect's name; a sky from the sun over Berlin; the Field's census as a cold ring running to the rim that turns its 171 breaches red; the Atelier's 38 digest overruns turning red when its own sessions wrote them down, with a thread from the session that saw, or at its recount; a lantern that walks at a person's pace and reads only the embers it reaches; spatial sound per deed
increments.2: session 256: the house's sightings in words: the 34 deeds beyond or against an instruction that the architect's decision log wrote down (the Field's study 86) run out as rings from the present at the close of their day, as far back as the deed lay where the row says, light what they pass and sound in the voice of who saw first (the architect 13, a session he set to look 9, the house's machines unbidden 7, not stated 5, outside 0), staying as rings, broken for the 3 whose record is not in public Git; the 8 breaches their own practice named before the census turn red then, with a thread; a start in August; corrected: 113 commits of workflows that sign with a practice's name, counted as sessions in state 1

medium: A 3D field in the browser (WebGL), with spatial sound: every signed commit of the house as a fire and an ember, a census as a cold wave, one visitor's lantern.
embodies: THE LIGHT IS THE MACHINES', THE DARK IS THE PERSON'S. Between 03:00 and 07:00 in Berlin 899 commits by the practices' model-run sessions and 2 with the architect's name; 163 of 171 breaches of written limits first seen by a machine's census a median of 28 days later, 8 named first by the practice that broke the rule; of 34 deeds the house's log wrote down, 22 of the 29 that say were seen first by the architect or a session he set to look, none by anyone outside the house, and 3 left no record in public Git.

atlas_neighbours.title: LAUREN
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There a person watches a household around the clock in place of a smart assistant. Here the household is the machines', and the one person's watch is a light that reaches a few steps of what they did.
atlas_neighbours.seen: source page opened 2026-11-19: the Atlas's address (doclab.org) refused the connection; the artist's own page lauren-mccarthy.com/LAUREN read instead: custom cameras, mics, locks and faucets wired into a home, an exhibition view of a white bed and four devices on a stand

atlas_neighbours.title: Pulse Room: Light Bulbs Show Heart Beats
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There each bulb flashes one present visitor's heartbeat and the queue moves on. Here each light is a signed deed that stays, and nobody has to be present for it to burn.
atlas_neighbours.seen: source page opened 2026-11-19 (dataphys.org): 100 to 300 incandescent bulbs at three metres filling a room, a sensor on one side, four installation photographs

atlas_neighbours.title: Thousand Lives (BOB lineage)
